name: Zain Dana Harper
description: Independent systems engineer, toolmaker, and natural philosopher in Kent, Washington. Five connected open-source platforms spanning deterministic compilers, AI verification, local frontier models, multi-backend rendering, and civic provenance.

author.name: Zain Dana Harper
author.background: Eleven years commercial arboriculture rigging and about thirteen years self-directed software, compiler, graphics, and empirical verification engineering.

flagships.name: BuildLang
flagships.summary: Rust-built compiled systems language with typed capability effects, 12 targets (C, HLSL, GLSL, WGSL, Metal, SPIR-V, x86-64, RISC-V, WASM), V5 superoptimizer, Universal Hourglass lowering, 1.18M-record corpus engine, BuildDB (BDB) checksummed SQL, and BuildTeX PDF typesetting.

flagships.name: The Flywheel
flagships.summary: Self-hosted AI workstation and coding harness consolidating 31 packages behind cryptographic offline receipts, Rowan orchestration, Three-Plate Verification Oracle (115/115 defect recall, 0 false accepts), EMET byte-integrity witnessing, and Articulate deterministic prose linting.

flagships.name: The Playground
flagships.summary: Unified creative field and rendering engine combining Estuary continuous Perret-lantern metamers, 35 creative engines (Loom, Posters, Studio, Fractals, Type Forge, Shaders, Retro 46 FX, Sound), Native RAW DX12/Vulkan/WebGPU (96/96 live Skyrim SE moving-camera pass), Low Water 3D game, and Superframe deterministic core.

flagships.name: The Commons (CMMNS)
flagships.summary: Local-first, account-free browser extension surfacing account provenance, coordination cues, Content Credentials (C2PA), and fact-checks across 9 social platforms.

flagships.name: Research, Local Frontier Models & Security
flagships.summary: 30 reproducible empirical studies (12 published nulls), 13 DOI-indexed Zenodo preprints, Local Frontier Model Lab (JFC3P-7B-Oracle, NOH-4, Plato-Key, AVTR-4R, FRESCO/MoLT), and capability-public security hierarchy.

verificationPolicy: Every empirical claim links to a reproducible local command or SHA-256 receipt. Negative and null results stay published beside positive results.
